registered_by: operator ruling 2026-09-20: 'the most robust production system' — a checkpoint that cannot be distinguished from its training set may not be selected
question: Can the policy's CHOICES be told apart from its evidence? (policy-side memorization; near-duplicate prompt detection is a separate, data-side guard)

statistics.choice_discrimination: total-variation distance between the empirical action distribution on in-sample prompts and on unseen prompts
statistics.outcome_gap_bp: mean(realized net bp | unseen) - mean(realized net bp | in-sample)
statistics.dose_response: Spearman rho between realized net bp and the number of times the prompt appeared in training (optional; requires repeat_count)

null: permutation: the in_sample labels are shuffled (N_PERM=400, seed=7) and each statistic is recomputed; the bound is the (1-ALPHA)=0.99 quantile
decision_rule: SUSPECTED if ANY statistic exceeds its permutation bound; SUSPECTED or insufficient_groups ⇒ the checkpoint is NOT selectable, and no fallback may substitute for the verdict
interpretation: A suspected run is reported and re-trained, never averaged in. A clean run is not proof of generalisation — it is the absence of a detectable exposure effect, which is the only thing this instrument can assert.
fail_closed: python memorization_detector.py --score ... returns rc=1 when the verdict is SUSPECTED, when the groups are too thin, or when no preregistered instrument is present; grpo_loop.run_gate refuses selection on any of those
records_producer: the RL evaluation step must score matched in-sample and unseen prompts through the SAME policy and write reports/MEMORIZATION_RECORDS.jsonl with {prompt_sha256, in_sample, chosen, realized_net_bp, repeat_count}
scope_note: the wall gate remains the primary selection signal: this instrument can only VETO, never promote
